Key Event

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:52pm

By Dean Bilton

Gold Coast did their work in the first half and put the cue in the rack for the second. In fact you could say the game was decided in 10 minutes of footy in the second quarter. Either side of that the game was pretty tight, and the Power had the better of it at times.

Did the Suns manage the game, keeping Port at arm's length throughout while seeing the job out? Or did they run out of gas and leave the door open, offering an opportunity a better team may have taken? It doesn't matter in the end, but it might in the future.

Port again weren't bad, and were brilliantly led by Zak Butters, but were outclassed in crucial moments by the Suns. They're a better team than a 3-7 record, but the ladder rarely lies.

Suns march on. Their incredible Darwin record continues.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:49pm

By Dean Bilton

That's Gold Coast's first goal of the last quarter, with only about 80 seconds left on the clock. That's a fine finish though on his wrong foot, snapping under pressure on the left.

Walter has been really good tonight. A big contributor to a Suns win.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:43pm

By Dean Bilton

Joe Richards missed a set shot from directly in front, and then Jack Whitlock couldn't finish from the top of the goalsquare. Either of those go through and things would be getting really squeaky for the Suns.

Now Georgiades has hit the post from an attempted bicycle kick at the top of the square. All happening.

Nineteen points is the margin with a little under six minutes to play. All Port right now.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:41pm

By Dean Bilton

Back to 22 points! The Suns are being punished for their lack of killer instinct here, and Port might just have a taste for it now.

Richards rushed that to his boot in congestion and squeezed it perfectly through the crowd. It's not done yet.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:37pm

By Dean Bilton

Good night to be a Port Adelaide Joe. Another free kick, this for a bit of an overzealous dump from Holman, hands Richards the shot on goal. He doesn't miss.

They've got nine minutes to kick five goals. Maybe?

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:35pm

By Dean Bilton

Caught high in the goal square, they don't come much easier than that for Berry. He's improving week to week.

It's a 35-point game with 10 minutes to play.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:34pm

By Dean Bilton

Ten minutes to play in the last term and we haven't had a goal in it yet. I reckon if the umpires offered to the teams they could shake hands and go home right now, they'd probably take that.

On a hot night with the result settled, there isn't much to gain for either of them right now.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:29pm

By Henry Hanson

As a Pies fan, did think this game was a danger game for Sydney. Could have been so much worse for the black and white, but they were far from embarassed. Kick straight in the 2nd quarter and we could well have caused a massive boilover.

- Jeremy

Far, far from a disappointing performance from the undermanned Pies.

Even at the time, it felt like that wasteful second quarter - in which the Magpies kicked 1.7 - would come back to bite Collingwood.

A 6.6 third term from the Swans ensured that it did.

Key Event

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:17pm

By Henry Hanson

James Rowbottom, playing his 150th game, makes the final, game sealing contribution for the Swans.

His tackle in the middle of the field secures his side a gritty, nervy, six-point victory at the SCG.

That's a big win for the Swans, who were pushed all the way by a really plucky Collingwood side.

After a very lacklustre first half, it's Sydney's third quarter effort that wins the day for the ladder-leaders.

They kicked six goals to two between half-time and 3QT as the rain eased at the SCG.

Tom Papley and Logan McDonald slotted two key goals each for the Swans, but it was Brodie Grundy who once again stood tallest for the league leaders.

He finished the day with 31 disposals and 21 hit-outs - a deserved player of the match.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:15pm

By Henry Hanson

The Swans are in possession as we head inside the final minute.

Sydney leads by six.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:14pm

By Henry Hanson

Tom Papley has a chance to seal things but can only muster a behind.

The clock tick on as Collingwood raids forward and Jamie Elliot takes a good sliding mark before nailing his set shot!

The margin is back to six points with one and a half minutes to play!!

Key Event

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:12pm

By Dean Bilton

Feels like the Suns are rather strolling to victory now. Not overly stretching themselves, but not overly challenged by Port either.

A 40-point margin is probably the least the Suns deserve. There's a good chance it blows out to a fair bit more than that in the last.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:11pm

By Henry Hanson

Malcolm Rosas pushes one into the 50. Collingwood have the numbers but they're caught on their heels as Tom Papley sneaks around the back of the contest and snaps home.

A sigh of relief at the SCG as the Swans go 11 points in front.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:09pm

By Henry Hanson

And there's a massive roar as Isaac Heeney comes back on for the game's finale.

Fair to say the crowd are in this one.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:07pm

By Henry Hanson

That's a schmick finish from Logan McDonald!

Facing away from goal, he picks the ball up at the edge of the goal square and manoeuvres his kick over his head and between the big sticks.

Pretty fun stuff and the Swans are back in front by five points.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:05pm

By Henry Hanson

William Edwards spills a mark on the edge of Sydney's defensive 50 and proceeds to give away a freekick in the tackle.

The Magpies are given a wonderful opportunity to retake the lead.

Jack Crisp steadies and kicks slightly to the right.

It's only a behind - but it's enough to put Collingwood back in front.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 10:00pm

By Dean Bilton

They needed that. It's a long way back from here, but if there is to be a comeback it has to start somewhere.

Andrew was pinned holding the ball in the Mackinlay tackle, and the dish off to Farrell was a good idea. He bombs one through from 50 and tries to get his teammates up and going.

It didn't work though. Ned Moyle cashes in on a downfield free kick and snaps his second of the night.

Fri 15 May 2026 at 6:39pm

Queensland Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie oversees state agency Economic Development Queensland. ( ABC News: Luke Bowden )

Property developer, David Trask, who owns land in a special state development area, has bid $50,000 for a lunch with the Queensland deputy premier.

The donation comes only two months after the LNP relaxed an eight-year ban on developers making contributions to political parties on a state level.

Mr Trask said donations ultimately do not mean anything except as a goodwill gesture to parties, and any approvals would be made in line with laws.

A developer has bid $50,000 for a lunch with Queensland Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie, whose state government agency oversees land in which the developer has an interest.

The developer, David Trask, made the successful bid as a donation at lunch on Friday for the ruling Liberal National Party, held at the Brisbane Convention Centre and dubbed "Delivering for Queensland Industry Update".

The donation comes only two months after the LNP relaxed an eight-year ban on developers making contributions to political parties on a state level.

Mr Trask told the ABC on Friday that he has made donations to both sides of politics previously.

Do you know more? Contact Liam Walsh on encrypted email or Signal or Jack McKay on email.

He said the reality was that politicians were not the actual people who made decisions, and the state agency that oversees development would only make decisions in line with laws.

"The donations don't mean anything," he said.

"The donations [are] purely a goodwill gesture to a political party that runs our state, or our federal politics."

Plans and approvals have been active for development at North Harbour near Caboolture for decades, Mr Trask said, adding the that Labor Party had also been favourable previously to the project.

The North Harbour Priority Development Area is near Caboolture. ( ABC News )

In May last year, the LNP declared part of the project to become a "priority development area" (PDA) under the purview of the powerful state agency Economic Development Queensland (EDQ), of which Mr Bleijie is the responsible minister.

A PDA is designed to speed up development and slash red tape. Mr Bleijie, at the time, flagged it would help build 3,700 new homes.

"While Labor tied up builders and councils in red tape, we're resetting the planning partnership with local councils and communities to deliver new housing," he said.

Some current flat scrubland in the area has been owned by Mr Trask's Trask Development Corporation for decades. Among ambitious plans is turning parts of North Harbour into an artificial marina with housing.

The final PDA is yet to be decided, with an interim plan in place. Mr Trask pointed out that Economic Development Queensland was still going through a series of studies associated with any development plan.

"It's my experience that it's not going to matter what I want," he said.

Mr Bleijie was listed as a keynote speaker at the "Delivering for Queensland Industry Update" on Friday, which was attended by mining-related figures and property developers.

The event on Friday was held at the Brisbane Convention and Exhibition Centre. ( Brisbane Convention and Exhibition Centre )

The bidding at the lunch started at $5,000, Mr Trask said. He said multiple people made bids that increased in $500 increments.

Mr Trask believed the future event would be held at a restaurant.

"To be perfectly honest mate, I didn't read the detail," he said.

The donation laws were overturned, taking effect in March, after the LNP decried an earlier ban on developer donations as a financial gerrymander.

It often pointed the finger at the Labor Party, which brought in the state-level ban, while still being able to take money from unions.

A flyer for the fundraising lunch. ( Supplied )

Mr Trask said he had a "fundamental issue with a government treating a tax-paying person like a criminal".

He said the earlier ban on developer donations was an example of one political party engaging in one-upmanship over another political party.

Mr Trask held out the prospect of donating to the Labor Party on a state level.

"That will depend on what their policy positions are at the time and if there's anything I see there of benefit to my business," he said.

Mr Bleijie's office on Friday referred to statements from Attorney General Deb Frecklington's office: "We've delivered on the position we took to the election to restore fairness and Queenslanders voted for it after they saw through Labor's disgraceful scare campaigns, which were bankrolled by the violent and misogynistic CFMEU."

EDQ told the ABC it operated within a state integrity framework so any conflicts of interest were identified and managed, and employees had to comply with codes of conduct.

"EDQ is not aware of any instance where a developer has attempted to link political donations to work involving EDQ," an agency spokeswoman said.

An LNP spokesperson said: "The Party strictly adheres to its compliance obligations."
